# Recognition of a Non‑EU/EEA Master's Degree to Work in Brussels

## 1. Is official recognition/equivalence always mandatory?

No — it depends on the type of job:

- **Private sector, non‑regulated profession**: Recognition is **not legally compulsory**.

citations.cited_text: Cela veut dire qu’un employeur peut décider de t’engager sans que tu aies besoin d’obtenir la reconnaissance de ton diplôme étranger. Mais tu auras tr...
citations.title: L'équivalence de diplôme étranger pour travailler en Belgique ...

content.text: An employer can decide to hire you without you needing to obtain recognition of your foreign diploma, but you will very likely need diploma recognition if you want to work in the public sector or in a publicly subsidised institution.

In practice, however, many private employers informally ask for it as proof of your level.

- **Public sector**: Recognition is **effectively mandatory**.

citations.cited_text: En revanche, l’équivalence ou la reconnaissance de votre diplôme est obligatoire pour exercer une profession réglementée OU non réglementée dans le **...
citations.title: Travailler en Belgique : équivalences et reconnaissances - Infor ...

content.text: The equivalence or recognition of your diploma is obligatory to exercise a regulated OR non-regulated profession in the public sector or in publicly subsidized institutions.
Concretely, regional/community civil-service rules state it explicitly:

citations.cited_text: Si votre diplôme a été obtenu à l'étranger, vous devez fournir une attestation d'équivalence au diplôme requis pour ce poste délivrée par la Fédératio...
citations.title: Related FAQs - Wallonie

content.text: if your diploma was obtained abroad, you must provide a certificate of equivalence to the diploma required for the position, issued by the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles.
- **Regulated professions** (doctor, architect, lawyer, nurse, psychologist, accountant, etc.): Recognition is **always mandatory**, regardless of sector.

citations.cited_text: Dans le cas des professions réglementées, il n’est pas possible d’exercer sans reconnaissance préalable.
citations.title: Comment reconnaître des diplômes étrangers en Belgique ?

content.text: In the case of regulated professions, it is not possible to practise without prior recognition.
As one source summarizes,

citations.cited_text:
Lorsqu’une profession n’est pas réglementée, il n’est pas obligatoire d’obtenir une reconnaissance professionnelle préalable pour pouvoir travailler.
...
citations.title: Comment reconnaître des diplômes étrangers en Belgique ?

content.text: when a profession is not regulated, it is not obligatory to obtain prior professional recognition in order to work.

So the short answer: **"always mandatory" only applies to regulated professions and to any public-sector/subsidised job; for ordinary private jobs it is a practical advantage, not a legal requirement.**

## 2. Which authority is competent for Brussels, and how is the choice made?

Belgium has **no single nationwide recognition authority** — competence is split by **language Community**, not by region, which creates a specific situation for bilingual Brussels.

**How you choose between them in Brussels:**

content.text: Because Brussels is bilingual, you may want to apply for recognition with NARIC or with FWB or with both. This depends on the organisation you want to work for, or study with and within which language community you want to develop professionally. Their requirements and processes are slightly different and it may be easier to get recognition from one system than the other, depending for example on your professional field.
Legally, there is no cross-recognition between the two systems:

A recognition of equivalence issued by one of the three communities in Belgium (...

content.text: a recognition of equivalence issued by one of the three communities in Belgium is not valid in the other communities in Belgium, because there is no legal regulation providing for mutual recognition — this means that employers can decide which community in Belgium you should apply to for recognition of your diploma.
Practical rule of thumb:

content.text: working in Brussels does not mean one Brussels-wide authority; the employer's language system or sector body may point you toward the Flemish or French-speaking route.

If you target a French-speaking employer/sector, apply to **Fédération Wallonie‑Bruxelles (CFWB)**; if a Flemish one, apply to **NARIC‑Vlaanderen**; if uncertain, you may apply to both to keep your options open.

## 3. How concepts/procedures differ by type of job

**a) Non-regulated private-sector job**
- Two possible outcomes are available from the CFWB/NARIC services:
 - *Level equivalence* ("équivalence de niveau"):

citations.cited_text:
L’équivalence de niveau
Une équivalence de niveau consiste à reconnaître le **niveau académique générique**, non pas le contenu d’un diplôme.

L’équiv...

content.text: an equivalence of level consists of recognizing the generic academic level; it attests that you completed higher education abroad and specifies its level relative to diplomas existing in the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles (higher education certificate, Bachelor's or Master's), without however recognizing the pedagogical content of your studies.
- *Specific-degree equivalence*:

citations.cited_text: L’équivalence de niveau atteste donc que vous avez fait des études supérieures à l’étranger et précise leur niveau par rapport aux diplômes qui existe...
citations.title: Travailler en Belgique : équivalences et reconnaissances - Infor ...

content.text: an equivalence to a specific degree recognizes the content of a foreign training as equivalent to that of the diploma issued in the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles.
- As noted above, this is **useful but optional** for a private non-regulated job; it mainly helps with salary scales and HR screening.

**b) Public-sector job**
- Here equivalence becomes a **hiring condition**, applied uniformly regardless of whether the target profession is regulated or not.

But a normal CFWB/NARIC equivalence remains the standard route.

**c) Regulated profession** (whether the employer is public or private)
- First step: get the **general academic equivalence/recognition** from the relevant Community authority (CFWB or NARIC‑Vlaanderen), as for any higher-education diploma.

## 4. Current official sources

- **CFWB / French Community (NARIC‑FWB)** – Service de la Reconnaissance académique et professionnelle des diplômes étrangers d'enseignement supérieur, Rue A. Lavallée 1, 1080 Brussels; website equisup.cfwb.be / enseignement.be/enic-naric ([enic-naric.net – Belgium French Community](https://www.enic-naric.net/page-Belgium-French-Community))
- **NARIC‑Vlaanderen (Flemish Community)** – Department of Education and Training (AHOVOKS), naric@vlaanderen.be, naric.be ([enic-naric.net – Belgium Flemish Community](https://www.enic-naric.net/page-belgium-flemish-community))
- **be.brussels** – official Brussels-Capital Region portal page "Equivalence of diplomas" (be.brussels/en/education-teaching/equivalence-diplomas)
- **Vlaanderen.be** – "Equivalence of foreign diplomas in the three communities of Belgium" (official Flemish government explanation of the non-mutual-recognition rule)
- **business.belgium.be** (FPS Economy) – "Profession réglementée: faire reconnaître ses qualifications professionnelles"
- **FPS Public Health (health.belgium.be)** – for medical/paramedical regulated professions
- **Selor** (federal civil-service selection office, selor.be) and regional civil-service FAQs (wallonie.be, ifapme.be) for public-sector conditions
- **EU regulated-professions database** (via business.belgium.be) for checking profession status

For your specific case, the practical path is: (1) check if your intended job/profession is regulated using the EU/SPF Economie database; (2) if regulated, contact the relevant professional order/FPS in addition to CFWB or NARIC; (3) if non-regulated and private-sector, an equivalence is optional but recommended; (4) if public-sector, apply for equivalence with CFWB (French-speaking track) or NARIC‑Vlaanderen (Dutch-speaking track) depending on the employer/sector you're targeting in Brussels.
